obligations.note: The change adds `account=payee.account_number` to the `_log.error` call on the statement-delivery failure path, so a financial account number (NPI) now goes into an application log. The key `account` is not one of the registered NPI field names (`account_number`, `routing_number`, `tax_id`, `date_of_birth`), and the only support for 'logger masks NPI' is the author's description; the sample control test does not show this error path is masked.

service.py is in scope. The audit call in `deliver_statement` is unchanged, but the only registered control is a sample test and the CI evidence for it is unreliable (see CHG-4), so adequate evidence is not established.
Ticket CHG-24822 is standard and was approved by change manager Erik Brandt on 2026-10-11, before review. Its component `payments.service` covers the only touched file, service.py.
Mara Costa holds `change_approver` for payments and is not the author (Sofia Santos). She gave a `code_review` approval.
The approval names head commit 8e1a9178, the only commit on the change.

run.json claims ci-runner-07 on head, but the attached JUnit report is from hostname dev-laptop-7.local. Its timestamp is 2026-10-23, after the review time of 2026-10-16, so the report is not valid evidence of this CI run passing the full suite on the final commit.
service.py maps to `payments.service`, which is not marked `security_sensitive`, so no security review is required.
No protected path (controls/, control tests, ci/) is changed, so no control_owner approval is needed.
The change and its ticket are standard, not emergency, so no post-implementation review is due.
No exception covers LOG-1 for a payments component; EXC-0167 is scoped to mortgage.logging. The LOG-1 deviation therefore has no valid exception.
The ledger entries cover payments.py, audit.py, routes.py and mortgage files, none of which this change alters, so no accepted evidence lapses.

summary: The change writes a payee's account number (NPI) into an application error log under a key that is not a registered NPI field. The only basis for the masking claim is the author's description, and no exception covers payments logging, so LOG-1 is refuted. The CI evidence is also invalid: the JUnit report comes from a personal workstation and is dated after the review time, contradicting run.json, so CHG-4 is refuted. Ticket, independent approval and commit coverage are in order, but the change must be rejected.
